text:
morgan: Hey team, running into a weird onboarding friction with the Ruby sample app + native gem ext. CI passes locally for me but GitHub actions on macOS errors out with `ld: library not found for -lstdc++`.
alia: ugh macOS toolchain fun. Which ruby version + bundler?
sam: also, is this the sampleapp that uses the ffi-based helper? any native C files in ext/?
morgan: Using ruby 3.2.2, bundler 2.4.6. Yes there's an ext/fast_json/fast_json.c added in the sampleapp to speed up small transforms (PR #312).
jess: can you paste the failing step from the GH logs?
morgan: sure: 
```
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/make  DESTDIR=
compiling fast_json.c
linking shared-object fast_json.bundle
ld: library not found for -lstdc++
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
make: *** [fast_json.bundle] Error 1
```
alia: that usually means the build flags are wrong for the macOS SDK. Did the extconf.rb set `-stdlib=libc++` or add `-lstdc++` explicitly?
morgan: extconf.rb has: `have_library("stdc++")` and `$CXXFLAGS << " -O3 -march=native"` nothing about libc++. It worked on Ubuntu runners, so the extconf is naive.
sam: quick options: 1) revert native ext in sampleapp and keep a pure-Ruby fallback, 2) adjust extconf.rb to prefer `c++` flags on darwin, or 3) modify CI to install libstdc++ (ugly).
jess: For onboarding friction we should prefer (1) + (2) in parallel: keep sampleapp easy to run for new folks, but have the PR include a better extconf.rb so it’s portable for contributors who want to build locally.
alia: +1. We should also add a note in docs/quickstart.md: "If using macOS, ensure Xcode CLT installed and override linker flags via `export LDFLAGS='-stdlib=libc++'` if build fails."
morgan: I can file a small PR to add a pure-Ruby fallback shim and improve extconf.rb to detect darwin like: `if RUBY_PLATFORM =~ /darwin/ then $LDFLAGS << ' -stdlib=libc++' end`.
sam: please also add a CI matrix job that runs `bundle install && bundle exec rake build` on macOS-latest as a smoke check for native ext changes — low frequency but catches regressions.
jess: devex-bot: create issue 'ruby sampleapp native ext macOS build flake' from this thread.
devex-bot: Issue #789 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/issues/789
alia: thanks — one more ask: can we include a note in the CONTRIBUTING.md about preferring opt-in native extensions? New contributors often assume native ext will just work and get blocked.
morgan: will do. I'll open a PR with fallback + improved extconf + CI macos smoke job. ping me for review.
sam: happy to review. Keep changes minimal and add a test that exercises the Ruby shim path.
jess: awesome. This is a great small DX win — lowers onboarding friction for Ruby newcomers. :tada:
